headline: Bill Gates warned on US television that criminals using powerful AI models without safeguards could cause many damaging surprises in cybersecurity within a year.
score_reason: Pool 7 kept: a prominent warning backed by security-industry figures, though it is a forecast in an interview, not a new incident.
importance_line: Businesses, banks and their customers could face more extortion and disruption from AI-assisted attackers within a year, but this is a forecast made in one interview, and the 89% figure comes from a security company's report on 2025, not from Gates.
summary: Fox News reports that Bill Gates, the Microsoft co-founder, told CNN's Jake Tapper on Sunday 11 Oct 2026 that criminals using the latest AI models without safeguards could bring "a lot of negative surprises" in cybersecurity over the next year, through extortion or attacks meant to disrupt financial markets, and that the nearer danger is misuse, not AI getting out of control, which he called years away. Fox adds that the security firm CrowdStrike's 2026 Global Threat Report found attacks by AI-enabled adversaries rose 89% in 2025 and that criminals now need an average of 29 minutes to spread through a compromised network.
notes: Read in full on Fox News; the interview is on CNN and was not opened. Gates's warning is a forecast; the CrowdStrike numbers are Fox's addition.
